attempts.hypothesis: The C0/C1/DEL/Cf strip removes every character that can break the single-line operator notice.
attempts.method: 400k-token randomized fuzz (alphabet including U+2028, U+2029, U+200B, U+00A0, U+202E, combining marks, astral chars, spaces/tabs/newlines) plus targeted probes of the line-separator characters.
attempts.evidence: 0 outputs contained a C0/C1/Cf character, 0 were blank, 0 exceeded 64 code points, 0 contained a lone surrogate - but 14,929 outputs contained U+2028/U+2029 (General_Category Zl/Zp, not Cf): displayProgram(['ls\u2028fake-notice']) returns 'ls\u2028fake-notice'. findings.message: docs/security.md describes a different whitelist than the one the revision enforces, so the 'exact scope' of the rendering is not documented. Applying the documented algorithm ('anything else gives its last path segment ... and everything after the first `:` or `@` of that name is dropped') to alice:hunter2@host yields 'alice', while displayProgram returns 'host' and tests/unit/routing-guards.test.ts now asserts 'host' - i.e. the paragraph still documents the pre-revision behaviour for the exact shape this revision changed. The IPv6-literal exemption (https://[::1]:3000/app -> [::1]:3000) and the port strip are not described at all (the documented rule gives '['), and nothing in tests/unit/docs-consistency.test.ts pins this paragraph.

AC-1's 'NO command text is stored or rendered' does not hold for a token with no ASCII `:`/`@`/`/`/`?`/`#`: the whitelist's structural reduction is a no-op and the whole token is rendered and stored. Verified end-to-end through the real /devcontainer host-exec handler (hostExecution.allow=false, ledger + notice trace): input 'FOO=sk-live-abcdef' produced ledger.recent() === ['FOO=sk-live-abcdef'], '1 host command attempt this session - most recent: FOO=sk-live-abcdef' and the notice 'first host command attempt this session: FOO=sk-live-abcdef'; AWS_PROFILE=prod, [sk-live-abc] (brackets dropped, value kept) and a full-width-punctuation DSN behave the same. The documented residual only covers 'a credential that a caller spells as the name itself ... which is not a shape a command line produces in practice', which does not describe a NAME=value assignment - the first token of an env-prefixed command line, and a shape this code explicitly anticipates ('argv[0] may be a WHOLE command line').

Malformed /devcontainer host-exec invocations are counted, and can consume the session's one-shot first-attempt announcement, only when host execution is withheld. Driving the real handler: allow=false with '' -> count 1, summary 'most recent: (no command)', notice 'first host command attempt this session: (no command)'; allow=false with '--argv' (flag without a value) -> count 1, 'most recent: --argv'; allow=true with the same two inputs -> count 0 ('no host commands in this session'), because on that path parseHostExecArgv fails before the runner. So the same operator input yields different attempt counts per configuration, and in the withheld configuration the announcement that AC-1 makes the session's early-warning signal can fire for a usage error, leaving the first real attempt unannounced.

Two whitelist branches still select a value rather than a name. (a) A bracket-wrapped token that is not an IPv6 literal renders its content verbatim because the unwrap path applies split(/[:@]/)[0], a no-op without a separator: displayProgram(['[sk-live-abc]']) -> 'sk-live-abc' (the rev-18 note claims 'nothing else is exempt'). (b) When a value sits after the last `@` of a scheme-less token it is taken as the host: 'x/no@S3CR3Tpw' -> 'S3CR3Tpw' and '[::1]:8080@S3CR3Tpw' -> 'S3CR3Tpw'. Both need the caller to spell a credential-shaped value in argv[0], but the code comment's 'no credential can survive this rule' is stronger than what the function does.

The strip list is C0/C1/DEL/Cf, so the Unicode line separators U+2028 and U+2029 (Zl/Zp) survive rendering and reach the operator notice and the /devcontainer status line: displayProgram(['ls\u2028fake-notice']) -> 'ls\u2028fake-notice' (a 400k-token fuzz found 14,929 such outputs and 0 C0/C1/Cf). CommonMark treats U+2028/U+2029 as line endings, so a crafted argv[0] can add a line to the notice the code comment already wants the operator to be able to trust - the same reason the Cf strip (U+202E) was added.

A token that carries a scheme prefix with an empty authority renders the blank placeholder instead of the scheme or the name: displayProgram(['DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock']) and displayProgram(['unix:///x']) both return '(no command)', while 'unix://host/x' returns 'host'. The operator then sees 'first host command attempt this session: (no command)' / 'most recent: (no command)' for a real command attempt, using the same text the function returns when argv is empty.

The revision updated the expectations of the 'drops userinfo in scheme-less, path-prefixed and multi-@ tokens' block to 'host' but left the comment above them, which now contradicts its own assertions: 'The whitelist stops at the first `:`/`@`, so these render the USERNAME - never the password' sits directly above four expectations of 'host'. A reader of the test (the file a reviewer trusts for the rendering contract) is told the opposite of what is asserted.
